text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. Developers often refactor to make their code easier to read and understand. For example, they might rename variables, break large functions into smaller ones, or remove duplicate code. The main goal is to keep the program's behavior exactly the same while making the code cleaner inside. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which is the extra work that builds up when code is written quickly without proper design. By refactoring regularly, teams can keep their projects healthy and easier to maintain in the future.
